1) the SI in the k-record values and k-record times can be computed in a closed form, 2) the SI in k-record data is related to the SI in sequential maxima, and 3) the SI in a sample from an ISP is related to the information in the k-record sample.
In summary, our research is concerned with
SI content of k-record data.
the SI in k-record values, the SI in k-records, and the SI content of the data from an inverse sample of fixed size.
the SI content of the k-record data, and its associated k-record times.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the k-record information is not a good substitute for the information in the original data.
the SI in the ISP k-record data is larger than the SI in the k-record times and upper k-record values, but smaller than the SI in lower k-record values.
the SI contained in the k-records is greater than the SI in the original data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of the k-record data, the information content of the data is a function of the number of observations in the sample, and is not a function of the sampling plan.
the SI content in k-record data can be expressed in terms of the SI of the data in which the k-th record is embedded.
the SI content of the k-record data is a function of the SI in the parent data, the number of observations in the parent data and the number of k-record values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of SI, the k-record data is more informative than the raw data, but the ISP data is less informative.
the information in the k-record values and times is very similar to the information in the original data.
the SI in the k-record values is a function of the SI in the original data.
